response: The prevalence of incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) is relatively low. Research suggests that obesity may be a contributing factor to the development of idiopathic misty mesentery, as it can lead to increased pressure and inflammation in the mesenteric fat, resulting in the characteristic "misty" appearance on CT scans. However, more studies are needed to confirm the exact relationship between obesity and idiopathic misty mesentery.
